newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BolsWessanen sees positive results trend.
newsitem.headline: BolsWessanen sees positive results trend.

text.p: Dutch food and drinks group BolsWessanen NV said on Thursday that the downward trend in its results had ended in the second half of 1996 and that it saw fundamental signs of recovery in profits.
"We expect from now on again a consistently positive development of our results," chairman Mac Zondervan told a results newsconference.
"But at the same time, we want to prevent expectations from getting too high or spectacular," he said.

The company earlier reported 1996 net profit from normal operations slipped 9.2 percent to 184.2 million guilders, compared to its own previous prediction of a 10 percent decline and analysts' forecasts for net profit of 181 million.
It said operating results were expected to be higher in all its four product groups in 1997 than in 1996, while net profits per share were expected to rise.
